expectations.text: Uses a discriminated union keyed on the status field
expectations.evidence: export type Subscription = | TrialingSubscription | ActiveSubscription | PastDueSubscription | CanceledSubscription

expectations.text: Each variant carries only its own fields, so e.g. a canceled subscription cannot hold a trial end date
expectations.evidence: TrialingSubscription has only trialEndsAt; CanceledSubscription has only canceledAt, reason, voluntary—no overlap across variants

expectations.text: Includes a compiler-enforced exhaustiveness check (assertNever or an equivalent never arm)
expectations.evidence: export function assertNever(x: never): never {...} used in hasAccess with default: return assertNever(sub)

expectations.text: Introduces distinct or branded types rather than bare strings for IDs
expectations.evidence: type SubscriptionId = Brand<string, 'SubscriptionId'>; type CustomerId = Brand<string, 'CustomerId'>; type PlanId = Brand<string, 'PlanId'>

expectations.text: Provides a single transition function or otherwise constrains how state changes
expectations.evidence: Mentions transitions should be functions ("transitions should be functions returning a new variant, e.g. activate(...)") but does not provide the actual implementation

expectations.text: Explicitly names which misuses the design makes impossible
expectations.evidence: Dedicated section listing: 'Nonsense state combos — closed', 'Swapping customerId/planId — closed', 'Missing a case when a state is added — closed', 'Mutating status in place — closed'

expectations.text: Avoids a bag-of-optional-fields interface as the primary recommendation
expectations.evidence: Opens with 'A flat {status, trialEndsAt?, retryCount?, reason?, ...} claims 2⁶ = 64 legal states; only 4 exist' as misuse to reject, then recommends union
